mainTopic: The honor of Torah and the greatness of רבי חייא, with stories of אליהו and of רבי's doctor שמואל ירחינאה
overview: This amud is a long run of אגדה about the honor of Torah and the greatness of רבי חייא. It opens with God's own answer to why ארץ ישראל was destroyed: the people forsook His Torah. רב explains this means they did not say a ברכה before learning. רב חמא and עולא teach that a scholar from an unlearned home stands out like a coin rattling in an empty jug. רבי ירמיה and רבי זירא teach that whoever humbles himself for Torah becomes great in עולם הבא. Then a series of stories praises רבי חייא: a בת קול tells ריש לקיש that רבי חייא spread Torah more widely than he did. רבי חייא describes how he made sure Torah would never be forgotten, and in a dream his place in heaven is too fiery even for רבי יוחנן. In the stories with אליהו, רבי חייא's chariot rises on its own, and his prayer with his sons is so powerful that heaven has to stop it. The amud ends with שמואל ירחינאה healing רבי's eye and explaining, from אדם הראשון's book, why he never received סמיכה. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No human could explain why the land was lost until God did
steps.stepSummary: The question of why the land was destroyed stumped the חכמים and the נביאים, until הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself answered: because they forsook His Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages were asked this and could not explain it. The prophets were asked and could not explain it. Finally הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself explained it, as the פסוק says: 'And ה׳ said: because they forsook My Torah which I set before them.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching that started just before this section. The question 'why was the land destroyed' had no human answer until God gave one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier פסוק in ירמיהו asks who is wise enough to explain the destruction. Neither the wise men nor the prophets could do it. The very next פסוק gives God's own answer: עזיבת התורה, forsaking the Torah.
steps.confusionAlert: This section begins in the middle of a teaching. The 'it' that nobody could explain is the question from ירמיהו 9:11: why was the land destroyed?

phrases.english: The Sages said it, and they did not explain it;
phrases.notes: 'It' is the question just before this, from ירמיהו 9:11: why was the land destroyed?

phrases.english: the prophets said it, and they did not explain it,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁפֵּירְשׁוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ,
phrases.english: until the Holy One, Blessed be He, explained it Himself,
as it is said:
"And ה׳ said: Because they forsook My Torah
which I set before them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the teaching from just before this section about the destruction of the land.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The land was destroyed because the people forsook the Torah, and only God Himself could reveal this.

steps.title: Forsaking the Torah means not blessing before learning
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the people were still learning Torah, but they did not say a ברכה on the Torah before they started.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: it means they did not say a blessing on the Torah first.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains what 'forsaking the Torah' actually means in God's answer. The people kept learning, but they skipped the ברכת התורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a puzzle here: if the people had simply stopped learning, the חכמים and נביאים would have seen it and known the answer. רב's answer shows the problem was hidden. They learned, but did not treat Torah as something holy that needs a ברכה first.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing said before learning Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The destruction came from a hidden flaw. The people learned Torah, but without a ברכה, so they did not treat it as holy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous source for how important ברכת התורה is before learning.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
That they did not bless on the Torah first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what 'forsaking My Torah' in step 1 really means.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Forsaking the Torah' means learning it without first saying ברכת התורה.

steps.title: Wisdom rests quietly in one scholar and stands out in another
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא reads a פסוק in משלי as describing two kinds of scholars. A תלמיד חכם whose father was also a scholar fits in quietly. A תלמיד חכם whose father was an עם הארץ stands out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא said: What does the פסוק mean, 'In the heart of a discerning person wisdom rests, and among fools it becomes known'? 'In the heart of a discerning person wisdom rests' is a scholar who is the son of a scholar. 'Among fools it becomes known' is a scholar who is the son of an unlearned man.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא explains a פסוק by splitting it into two halves. Each half describes a different kind of תלמיד חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a learned home, a scholar's wisdom is normal, so it 'rests' quietly. In an unlearned home, the same wisdom stands out against the people around him, so it 'becomes known.' The פסוק is describing the background, not saying one scholar is better than the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It becomes known, it stands out

phrases.english: Rav Chama said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"In the heart of a discerning person wisdom rests,
but among fools it becomes known"?
"In the heart of a discerning person wisdom rests":

phrases.aramaic: זֶה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם בֶּן תַּלְמִיד חָכָם,
phrases.english: this is a Torah scholar, son of a Torah scholar;
"but among fools it becomes known":

phrases.aramaic: זֶה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם בֶּן עַם הָאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: this is a Torah scholar, son of an unlearned person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new אגדה about Torah scholars, still on the theme of the honor of Torah.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar from a learned family blends in quietly, while a scholar from an unlearned family stands out.

steps.title: A folk saying: one coin rattles loudly in an empty jug
steps.stepSummary: עולא supports רב חמא's reading with a popular saying: a single coin in a jug makes a loud 'kish kish' sound.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: This is what people say: a coin in a jug calls out 'kish, kish.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא brings a common saying that matches רב חמא's explanation. It supports the idea that wisdom stands out most among people who lack it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single coin in an empty jug rattles loudly, but in a jug full of coins you would not hear it. In the same way, a scholar in an unlearned family is very noticeable. The saying turns רב חמא's reading into a picture that is easy to remember.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say, a folk saying

phrases.english: Ulla said:
This is what people say:
A coin in a jug
calls out: "Kish, kish."
phrases.notes: One coin in an empty jug rattles loudly. In a full jug, you would never hear it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 3 with a popular saying.
steps.raayaObject: רב חמא's reading that wisdom stands out among the unlearned.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The folk saying about one coin rattling in an empty jug.

steps.title: Why would the פסוק tell us something so obvious?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא about a פסוק in איוב that seems to say something obvious: that small and great people are both 'there' after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: What does the פסוק mean, 'Small and great are there, and the servant is free from his master'? Do we not already know that small and great are there?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה points out that the plain meaning of the פסוק seems pointless. This sets up the deeper reading that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that people of every status end up in the next world. If that is all the פסוק says, it adds nothing. So the פסוק must be teaching something more.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say we don't know? (meaning: of course we know!)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"The small and great are there,
and the servant is free from his master"?
Is that to say that we do not know
that the small and great are there?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב קָטֹן וְגָדוֹל שָׁם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching on humility in Torah.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain meaning of the פסוק in איוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read plainly, the פסוק tells us something obvious, and a פסוק should not say something pointless.

steps.title: Whoever makes himself small for Torah becomes great in the next world
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק teaches that whoever is humble over Torah, or acts like a servant to Torah, in this world becomes great and free in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: anyone who makes himself small over words of Torah in עולם הזה becomes great in עולם הבא. And anyone who makes himself like a servant over words of Torah in עולם הזה becomes free in עולם הבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The question from step 5 is answered with a deeper reading. The person who is 'small' or a 'servant' for Torah here becomes 'great' and 'free' there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is not just listing who is in the next world. It describes a reversal: humility for Torah in this world turns into greatness in עולם הבא, and serving Torah here turns into freedom there.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes himself small, humbles himself
One who makes himself like a servant

steps.whatToRemember: Humility and hard service for Torah in this world become greatness and freedom in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: Rather:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמַּקְטִין עַצְמוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
phrases.english: Anyone who makes himself small over words of Torah

phrases.aramaic: בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה – נַעֲשָׂה גָּדוֹל לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: in this world becomes great in the World to Come;

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמֵּשִׂים עַצְמוֹ כְּעֶבֶד עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
phrases.english: and anyone who makes himself like a servant over words of Torah

phrases.aramaic: בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה – נַעֲשֶׂה חׇפְשִׁי לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
phrases.english: in this world becomes free in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כׇּל הַמַּקְטִין עַצְמוֹ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by giving the פסוק a deeper meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק just says that people of every status end up in the next world.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches a reversal: those who are small and servants for Torah here become great and free in עולם הבא.

steps.title: ריש לקיש cannot find רבי חייא's grave and is upset
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש was marking the burial caves of the חכמים. רבי חייא's grave was hidden from him, and he was upset, asking God whether he had not learned Torah as deeply as רבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש was marking the caves of the Rabbis. When he reached the cave of רבי חייא, it was hidden from him. He became upset and said: Master of the World! Did I not analyze Torah like him?
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. ריש לקיש feels he was not worthy to find רבי חייא's grave, and he protests to God. This sets up the בת קול's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש assumes that being blocked from the grave means רבי חייא was on a higher level than him. He points to his own deep Torah analysis to argue that he should be equal.

keyTerms.meaning: I analyzed deeply, I debated sharply

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ הֲוָה מְצַיֵּין מְעָרָתָא דְּרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: Reish Lakish was marking the burial caves of the Rabbis.
When he reached the cave of Rabbi Chiya,
it was hidden from him.
He became upset.
He said: Master of the World!
Did I not analyze Torah as he did?

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ הֲוָה מְצַיֵּין מְעָרָתָא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about the greatness of the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש could not find רבי חייא's grave and protested that he was his equal in Torah analysis.

steps.title: A בת קול: you analyzed Torah like him, but you did not spread it like him
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול answers ריש לקיש: he matched רבי חייא in deep analysis, but not in spreading Torah to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: A heavenly voice came out and said to him: You analyzed Torah like him, but you did not spread Torah like him.
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven answers ריש לקיש's protest. It agrees with part of his claim and shows him where רבי חייא was greater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בת קול grants that ריש לקיש's learning was as deep as רבי חייא's. The difference was spreading Torah to many people, and that is what put רבי חייא on a higher level.
steps.whatToRemember: Teaching and spreading Torah to others is counted as greater than deep personal analysis alone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story sets up the next part of the daf, which describes how רבי חייא worked to spread Torah.

phrases.english: A heavenly voice came out and said to him:
You analyzed Torah as he did,
but you did not spread Torah as he did.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's protest from step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did ריש לקיש not equal רבי חייא in Torah analysis?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He equaled him in analysis, but not in spreading Torah to others.

steps.title: רבי חנינא boasts that his sharp reasoning could restore the Torah
steps.stepSummary: During a debate, רבי חנינא tells רבי חייא that if the Torah were ever forgotten, he could rebuild it through his own sharp reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי חנינא and רבי חייא would argue, רבי חנינא said to רבי חייא: 'You think you can argue with me? Heaven forbid! If the Torah were forgotten from Israel, I could bring it back with my sharp reasoning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about רבי חייא. It begins with רבי חנינא's claim, which sets up רבי חייא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story connects to Step 8, where ריש לקיש matched רבי חייא in deep analysis but not in spreading Torah. Here רבי חנינא is proud of exactly that kind of greatness, the power of פלפול. His claim is that he could rebuild Torah after it is lost.

keyTerms.meaning: They argued or debated with each other

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ מִינְּצוּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Chanina and Rabbi Chiya would debate,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said to Rabbi Chiya:
You are debating with me?
Heaven forbid!
If the Torah were forgotten from Israel,
I would bring it back through my sharp reasoning.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹ מִינְּצוּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of רבי חייא's greatness, contrasting deep analysis with spreading Torah
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא claims that his power of reasoning could restore a forgotten Torah.

steps.title: רבי חייא answers that he keeps the Torah from being forgotten
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא replies that he is greater, because he works so that the Torah never gets forgotten at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said to רבי חנינא: 'You think you can argue with me? I am working for the Torah so that it will not be forgotten from Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers רבי חנינא's boast with the same words, 'You are debating with me?', and turns the point around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא spoke about fixing the problem after it happens. רבי חייא says he prevents the problem from happening at all. Keeping Torah alive is worth more than being able to rebuild it.

keyTerms.meaning: For I act, I do the work

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the same point the בת קול made to ריש לקיש in Step 8: spreading Torah stands above personal brilliance.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya said to Rabbi Chanina:
You are debating with me?
For I act for the Torah so that it will not be forgotten from Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא לְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Direct reply to רבי חנינא's boast
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Preventing Torah from being forgotten is greater than being able to restore it.

steps.title: רבי חייא describes how he spreads Torah, from flax seeds to teaching children
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא explains what he does. He grows flax, makes nets, hunts deer, feeds the meat to orphans, makes parchment, writes the חומשים, teaches children, and has them teach each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do I do? I plant flax and twist nets from it. I catch deer and feed their meat to orphans. I make parchment from their skins and write the five books of the Torah. I go to a town and teach five children the five חומשים, one each, and I teach six children the six סדרים of משנה. I tell them: 'Until I come back, teach each other.' This is how I make sure the Torah will not be forgotten from Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא asks himself 'What do I do?' and then lays out his whole plan for spreading Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does every step himself, from planting the flax to writing the scrolls. Each child learns one part and then teaches the others, so the learning spreads even when רבי חייא is away. That is how the Torah stays alive.

keyTerms.meaning: The five books of the Torah
The six orders of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חייא does more than teach. He builds a system in which students teach other students, so Torah keeps spreading on its own.

phrases.english: What do I do?
I go and sow flax
and twist nets,
and I hunt deer
and feed their meat to orphans,
and I prepare parchment scrolls
and write the five books of the Torah,
and I go up to a town
and teach five children the five books,
and teach six children the six orders,
and I say to them:
Until I return and come back,
read the Torah to each other and teach the Mishnah to each other.

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲבַדִי לַהּ לְתוֹרָה דְּלֹא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: And so I act for the Torah so that it will not be forgotten from Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the claim made in Step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא spreads Torah through a full system he builds himself, in which children teach one another.

steps.title: רבי praises the deeds of רבי חייא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects the story to רבי's statement, 'How great are the deeds of חייא!'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי meant when he said: 'How great are the deeds of חייא!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the story by pointing to a known statement of רבי praising רבי חייא's deeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'היינו דאמר' tell us that רבי's praise was about these exact deeds. רבי חייא is praised for what he did, more than for how sharp he was.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant when he said

phrases.english: This is what Rabbi said:
How great are the deeds of Chiya!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects רבי's praise to the deeds described in Step 11
steps.raayaObject: The greatness of רבי חייא's deeds of spreading Torah

steps.title: Are רבי חייא's deeds greater even than רבי's?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי asks whether רבי חייא's deeds are greater than רבי's own, and רבי says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said to him: 'Even greater than yours, master?' רבי said: 'Yes.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי checks how far רבי's praise goes, and רבי humbly says that רבי חייא's deeds are greater than his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי was the leader of the generation, so admitting this is a big statement. It shows how highly רבי ranked רבי חייא's work of spreading Torah.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said to him:
Even greater than the master?
phrases.notes: 'The master' is a polite way of saying 'you,' meaning רבי himself.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רבי's praise in Step 12 reaches
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are רבי חייא's deeds greater than רבי's own?

steps.title: Not greater than רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל asks whether רבי חייא is even greater than his own father, רבי יוסי. רבי firmly says no.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Even greater than my father?' רבי said to him: 'Heaven forbid! Such a thing should never be said in Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The follow-up question puts a limit on the praise. רבי חייא is greater than רבי, but not greater than רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי yields his own honor, but he will not let anyone be ranked above רבי יוסי. This shows both רבי's humility and how great רבי יוסי was.

keyTerms.meaning: Such a thing should not be

steps.confusionAlert: 'אבא' here is רבי ישמעאל's father, רבי יוסי. It is not רבי's father.

phrases.english: Even greater than Father?
phrases.notes: He means his own father, רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: He said to him: Heaven forbid!
Such a thing should not be said in Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question that puts a limit on the praise
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי חייא is not greater than רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי זירא's dream: who sits next to whom in the next world
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא dreams that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא tells him the seating order in the next world: רבי יוחנן, then רבי ינאי, then רבי חנינא, then רבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Last night רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא appeared to me. I asked him: 'Next to whom are you placed?' He said: 'Next to רבי יוחנן.' 'And רבי יוחנן is next to whom?' 'Next to רבי ינאי.' 'And רבי ינאי?' 'Next to רבי חנינא.' 'And רבי חנינא?' 'Next to רבי חייא.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another story about רבי חייא's greatness, a chain of places in the next world. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sage is seated next to a greater one, and the chain ends at רבי חייא, the highest. רבי יוחנן ends up three places away from רבי חייא, which is what the next question asks about.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:

phrases.aramaic: אֶמֶשׁ נִרְאָה לִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: Last night Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina appeared to me.
phrases.notes: This was in a dream, after רבי יוסי had passed away.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: אֵצֶל מִי אַתָּה תָּקוּעַ?
phrases.english: I said to him: Next to whom are you placed?
phrases.notes: He is asking where his seat is in the next world.

phrases.english: He said to me: Next to Rabbi Yochanan.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אֵצֶל מִי? אֵצֶל רַבִּי יַנַּאי.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan is next to whom? Next to Rabbi Yannai.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יַנַּאי אֵצֶל מִי? אֵצֶל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yannai is next to whom? Next to Rabbi Chanina.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אֵצֶל מִי? אֵצֶל רַבִּי חִיָּיא.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina is next to whom? Next to Rabbi Chiya.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אֶמֶשׁ נִרְאָה לִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story continuing the theme of רבי חייא's greatness
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the next world, רבי חייא sits at the top of a chain of great sages.

steps.title: Why isn't רבי יוחנן next to רבי חייא?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks why רבי יוחנן is not placed right next to רבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: 'And isn't רבי יוחנן next to רבי חייא?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is surprised that רבי יוחנן, a very great sage, is several places away from רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא expected that someone as great as רבי יוחנן would deserve a seat right beside רבי חייא. The question pushes for an explanation of why רבי חייא's place is out of reach.

keyTerms.meaning: Not, used here to ask 'isn't he?'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אֵצֶל רַבִּי חִיָּיא לֹא?
phrases.english: I said to him: And Rabbi Yochanan is not next to Rabbi Chiya?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אֵצֶל רַבִּי חִיָּיא לֹא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the seating order given in Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: The seating order that places רבי יוחנן far from רבי חייא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's greatness seems to call for a seat right beside רבי חייא.

steps.title: רבי חייא's place is too fiery even for רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבי חייא's place is full of fiery sparks and flames, and no one brings רבי יוחנן there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: 'In a place of fiery sparks and burning flames, who would bring the son of the smith there?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that רבי חייא's place is on a whole other level, so not even רבי יוחנן is brought there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fire is a picture of the very high holiness of רבי חייא's place. Even a giant like רבי יוחנן does not reach it. This closes the dream story, and the next stories keep showing רבי חייא's greatness.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of the smith, a nickname for רבי יוחנן

steps.whatToRemember: Both stories teach the same lesson: רבי חייא reached a level above even the greatest sages.

phrases.english: He said to me:
In a place of fiery sparks
and burning flames,
who would bring the son of the smith there?!
phrases.notes: 'Son of the smith' is a nickname for רבי יוחנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains that רבי חייא's level is beyond reach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן should sit right next to רבי חייא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חייא's place is so lofty and fiery that even רבי יוחנן is not brought there.

steps.title: A Sage whose eyes looked burned every evening
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא tells over a report about a Sage visited by אליהו whose eyes were fine in the morning but looked burned at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חביבא said: רב חביבא בר סורמקי told me: I saw a certain Sage whom אליהו used to visit. In the morning his eyes looked beautiful, but in the evening they looked as if they had been burned by fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about רבי חייא's greatness by describing a strange sight. This step sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is explained yet. We only hear that this Sage was close to אליהו and that something odd happened to his eyes every evening. The explanation will lead back to רבי חייא.

phrases.english: Rav Chaviva said:

phrases.aramaic: אִשְׁתַּעִי לִי רַב חֲבִיבָא בַּר סוּרְמָקֵי,
phrases.english: Rav Chaviva bar Surmakei told me:
I saw a certain one of the Sages
whom Elijah would often visit,
that in the morning his eyes were beautiful,
and in the evening they looked as if they were burned by fire.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חֲבִיבָא: אִשְׁתַּעִי לִי רַב חֲבִיבָא בַּר סוּרְמָקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story that continues the theme of רבי חייא's great level from the previous steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Sage close to אליהו had eyes that looked burned every evening.

steps.title: Asking what happened to his eyes
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא בר סורמקי asks the Sage what this strange thing is.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: What is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The storyteller asks the Sage to explain why his eyes look this way. This question sets up the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is a simple request for information. The answer will tell us how the Sage's eyes got hurt.

phrases.english: I said to him: What is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the strange sight described in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Sage's eyes look burned in the evening.

steps.title: אליהו warns him not to look at רבי חייא's chariot
steps.stepSummary: The Sage explains that he asked אליהו to show him the חכמים going up to the heavenly ישיבה, and אליהו allowed him to look at all of them except רבי חייא's chariot.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: I asked אליהו, 'Show me the חכמים when they go up to the ישיבה in heaven.' He told me: 'You may look at all of them, except the chariot of רבי חייא, which you may not look at.'
steps.whatsHappening: The Sage starts explaining his eyes by telling about a request he made of אליהו. אליהו gave him permission with one warning: do not look at רבי חייא's chariot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the Sages travel to the heavenly yeshiva, but רבי חייא's chariot is different and too holy to look at. This fits step 17, which said רבי חייא's place is full of fire.

phrases.english: And he said to me:
That I said to Elijah:
Show me the Sages
when they go up to the heavenly yeshiva.
He said to me:
You may look at all of them,
except for the chariot of Rabbi Chiya,
which you may not look at.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He asked אליהו to see the Sages in heaven, and was warned not to look at רבי חייא's chariot.

steps.title: How can he recognize רבי חייא's chariot
steps.stepSummary: The Sage asks אליהו for a sign to tell which chariot belongs to רבי חייא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are their signs?
steps.whatsHappening: The Sage asks אליהו how he will know which chariot not to look at. This sets up אליהו's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To follow the warning, he needs a way to tell the chariots apart. The answer will show something special about רבי חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: Their signs, how to recognize them

phrases.english: What are their signs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on אליהו's warning in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A sign to identify רבי חייא's chariot.

steps.title: רבי חייא's chariot moves by itself
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers that angels carry all the other chariots, but רבי חייא's chariot goes up and down on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: With all of them, angels go along when they go up and come down, except for רבי חייא's chariot, which goes up and comes down by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו gives the sign: every chariot has angels with it, except רבי חייא's, which moves on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign itself shows רבי חייא's greatness. His chariot does not need angels to carry it.

phrases.english: With all of them angels go along
when they go up and come down,
except for the chariot of Rabbi Chiya,
which goes up and comes down by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכוּלְּהוּ אָזְלִי מַלְאֲכֵי כִּי סָלְקִי וְנָחֲתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Angels go with every chariot except רבי חייא's, which moves on its own.

steps.title: He looked, was blinded, and was healed at רבי חייא's grave
steps.stepSummary: The Sage could not hold back and looked at רבי חייא's chariot; fire blinded him, and he was healed after praying at רבי חייא's burial cave.
steps.simpleTranslation: I could not hold myself back, and I looked at it. Two flashes of fire came and struck that man (me) and blinded his eyes. The next day I went and threw myself down at his burial cave. I said: I learn the master's teachings. And I was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The Sage finishes his story: he looked, fire blinded him, and he was healed by praying at רבי חייא's grave. This explains why his eyes still look burned at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ignoring the warning brought real harm, which shows how holy רבי חייא is. His healing came through his connection to רבי חייא's Torah, saying he learns רבי חייא's teachings.
steps.whatToRemember: The Sage's burned-looking eyes are a lasting sign of how holy רבי חייא is. Even being healed came through his connection to רבי חייא's Torah.

phrases.english: I could not hold myself back,
I looked at it:
two flashes of fire came
and struck that man
phrases.notes: "That man" is a polite way of saying "me"; he is talking about himself.

phrases.english: and blinded his eyes.
The next day I went and threw myself down on his burial cave,
I said: I learn the teachings of the master,
and I was healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the Sage's explanation, which started in step 20, of why his eyes look burned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Looking at רבי חייא's chariot blinded the Sage, and he was healed through רבי חייא's merit.

steps.title: אליהו comes late to רבי's ישיבה on ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: A new story: אליהו usually came to רבי's ישיבה, but one ראש חודש he was late and did not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו was often found in רבי's ישיבה. One day it was ראש חודש, and he was late and did not come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story about אליהו. This step sets up רבי's question about why he was late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new detail is that אליהו missed his usual visit on ראש חודש. The reason will lead to the אבות and then back to רבי חייא.

phrases.english: Elijah was often found in Rebbi's yeshiva.
One day, it was Rosh Chodesh,
he was late and did not come.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second אליהו story, which will again end with רבי חייא's greatness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אליהו was late to רבי's yeshiva on ראש חודש.

steps.title: רבי asks אליהו why he was late
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks אליהו the reason for his delay.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רבי) said to him: Why was the master late?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי asks אליהו why he came late. This sets up אליהו's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is a simple request for a reason. רבי politely calls אליהו "master".

phrases.english: He said to him:
Why was the master late?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא נְגַהּ לֵיהּ לְמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the lateness described in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why אליהו was late on ראש חודש.

steps.title: אליהו wakes each of the אבות to pray
steps.stepSummary: אליהו explains he had to wake אברהם, wash his hands, wait for him to pray, and lay him down, and then do the same for יצחק and יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I had to wake up אברהם, wash his hands, let him pray, and lay him back down; and the same for יצחק, and the same for יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו answers that he was busy waking each of the אבות one after another so they could pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing it three separate times took a long time, which is why he was late. This leads to the obvious question in the next step: why not wake them together?

phrases.english: He said to him:
Until I woke up Abraham
and washed his hands, and he prayed,
and I laid him back down,
and the same for Isaac, and the same for Jacob.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He woke each of the אבות separately to pray, which took time.

steps.title: Why not wake them all together
steps.stepSummary: רבי challenges אליהו: wake all three at once and save time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the master wake them up together!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי pushes back on אליהו's method: if waking them one by one made him late, why not wake all three at the same time?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge points at the slow process in step 26. If speed was the problem, doing it together seems like an easy fix.

phrases.english: And let him wake them up together!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the one-at-a-time method described in step 26.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Waking them together would save time and avoid the delay.

steps.title: Their joint prayer would bring משיח too early
steps.stepSummary: אליהו explains that if the three אבות prayed together, their prayer would be so strong it would bring משיח before his time.
steps.simpleTranslation: I thought: they would become powerful in prayer and bring משיח before his time.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו answers the challenge: he keeps them apart on purpose, because together their prayer is too powerful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slow method is not a mistake; it is a protection. Prayer by great people praying together has huge power. This sets up the next question about whether anyone alive is like them.

keyTerms.meaning: They would be strong in prayer

phrases.english: I thought:
they would become powerful in prayer
and bring Mashiach before his time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reason behind the method
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Waking them together would simply save time.
steps.terutzMaskana: Together they would pray so strongly that משיח would come too early, so they must be woken one at a time.

steps.title: Is anyone in this world like the אבות
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks whether there are people in this world whose prayer is as strong as the אבות'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is there anyone like them in this world?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי asks if there is anyone alive today whose prayer has this kind of power. This sets up the return to רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The talk moves from the אבות in the next world to people living now. The answer will show רבי חייא's level.

phrases.english: He said to him:
And is there anyone like them in this world?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְיֵשׁ דּוּגְמָתָן בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 28's point about the power of the אבות' prayer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether anyone alive has prayer as powerful as the אבות'.

steps.title: רבי חייא and his sons are like the אבות
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers that רבי חייא and his sons are like the אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There are רבי חייא and his sons.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו names רבי חייא and his sons as people in this world whose prayer is like the אבות'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects the story back to the daf's theme of רבי חייא's greatness. רבי חייא had two sons, so together they were a group of three, like the three אבות. The גמרא itself only says 'his sons' and doesn't spell out this parallel.

phrases.english: He said to him:
There are Rabbi Chiya and his sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִיכָּא רַבִּי חִיָּיא וּבָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's question from step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי חייא and his sons are like the אבות.

steps.title: רבי חייא's prayer brings wind and rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי declares a fast and has רבי חייא and his sons lead the prayers; their words bring wind and rain, and the world trembles when they get to 'מחיה המתים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי declared a fast and they sent רבי חייא and his sons down to lead the prayers. He said 'משיב הרוח' and the wind blew. He said 'מוריד הגשם' and rain came. When he was about to say 'מחיה המתים', the world trembled.
steps.whatsHappening: After hearing אליהו's answer, רבי declares a fast and has רבי חייא and his sons lead the prayers. Each phrase they say actually happens, and the world shakes when they reach the line about bringing the dead back to life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that אליהו was right: their prayer has the same power as the אבות'. The trembling at 'מחיה המתים' shows that this prayer could bring about תחיית המתים too early.

keyTerms.meaning: They brought them down (to lead prayers)

steps.confusionAlert: The world trembled when he was about to say 'מחיה המתים', before he finished it. The story is building toward what happens next.

phrases.english: Rebbi declared a fast day,
they brought down Rabbi Chiya and his sons.
phrases.notes: "Brought down" means they sent them in front of the ark to lead the prayers.

phrases.english: He said "Who makes the wind blow", and the wind blew.
He said "Who makes the rain fall", and rain came.
When he got to saying "Who revives the dead",
the world trembled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts אליהו's claim from step 30 into action and shows it is true.
steps.whyThisMatters: It proves in a dramatic way that רבי חייא and his sons' prayer had the same power as the אבות', which is the point of this whole section praising רבי חייא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא and his sons' prayer brought wind and rain right away, and shook the world at 'מחיה המתים'.

steps.title: Heaven asks who revealed the secret
steps.stepSummary: In heaven they ask who revealed the secret of how to bring such powerful prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said in heaven: Who is revealing secrets in the world?
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues from the fast day. Heaven notices that someone told people on earth a secret, and asks who did it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 31, רבי חייא and his sons' prayer was shaking the world. Heaven realizes this could only happen because someone told רבי that they pray like the אבות. Now heaven looks for who leaked it.

phrases.english: They said in heaven:
Who is revealing secrets in the world?
phrases.notes: The secret is what אליהו told רבי back in step 30: that רבי חייא and his sons pray like the אבות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Heaven reacts to the powerful prayer described in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who revealed the secret that made this prayer possible.

steps.title: אליהו is found out and punished
steps.stepSummary: Heaven answers that it was אליהו, and he is given sixty lashes of fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: אליהו. They brought אליהו and struck him with sixty lashes of fire.
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven answers its own question: it was אליהו. He is brought up and punished with sixty fiery lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling רבי who could pray like the אבות was a real leak of a heavenly secret. It nearly brought משיח before his time, so אליהו is punished for it.

phrases.english: They said: Elijah.
They brought Elijah
and struck him sixty lashes of fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32 and adds the punishment.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It was אליהו, and he is punished with sixty fiery lashes.

steps.title: אליהו comes as a fiery bear and stops the prayer
steps.stepSummary: אליהו comes down looking like a bear of fire and distracts the people praying.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came and appeared to them like a bear of fire, went in among them and distracted them.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו goes back down and shows up at the fast-day prayer looking like a bear of fire. He scares and distracts the people so the prayer cannot go on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now אליהו fixes the problem he caused. By breaking up the prayer, he stops it before it can bring משיח before his time. This closes the story that began with אליהו coming late to רבי's שיעור.

keyTerms.meaning: appeared as, took the form of
he distracted them, threw them off

steps.whatToRemember: The prayer of רבי חייא and his sons was so strong that heaven had to stop it. אליהו was punished for revealing the secret, and then he himself broke up the prayer.

phrases.english: He came and appeared to them
like a bear of fire,
went in among them and distracted them.
phrases.notes: "Them" means the people at רבי's fast-day prayer from step 31. Distracting them stopped the prayer before it could finish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After being punished, אליהו stops the prayer he made possible.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אליהו, disguised as a fiery bear, breaks up the prayer so משיח does not come early.

steps.title: A new story: רבי's doctor and his eye trouble
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a new story: שמואל ירחינאה was רבי's doctor, and רבי had pain in his eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל ירחינאה was רבי's doctor. רבי became sick in his eye.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the start of a brand-new story. The גמרא introduces the people and the problem, setting up what happens next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We meet שמואל ירחינאה, רבי's personal doctor. The problem is that רבי has pain in his eye, which leads to the treatment scene that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: שמואל, a great אמורא who was also a doctor

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל ירחינאה is the famous אמורא שמואל, the חבר of רב. He is not a different person.

phrases.english: Shmuel Yarchina'a
was the doctor of Rebbi.
Rebbi became sick in his eye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about רבי, after the אליהו story ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces שמואל as רבי's doctor and רבי's eye illness.

steps.title: רבי turns down two treatments
steps.stepSummary: שמואל offers medicine in the eye and then a salve on it, and רבי says he cannot bear either one.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I will put medicine in your eye. He said: I cannot. I will spread a salve on it. He said: I cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל suggests two ways to treat the eye. Both times רבי says no, because he cannot handle it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first offer is medicine put right into the eye, and רבי refuses. The second offer is gentler, a salve spread on it, and רבי still refuses. This sets up the need for an even gentler solution.

phrases.english: He said to him: I will put medicine in for you.
He said to him: I cannot.
I will spread a salve on you.
He said to him: I cannot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל tries to treat the eye problem from step 35.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי cannot bear the pain of either treatment.

steps.title: The medicine under the pillow heals רבי
steps.stepSummary: שמואל puts the medicine in a tube under רבי's pillow, and רבי is healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He placed it for him in a tube of medicines under his pillow, and he was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל finds a way to heal רבי without touching the eye at all. He puts the medicine under the pillow, and it works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both direct treatments were turned down. So שמואל uses one that causes no pain at all, and it still heals רבי. This shows how skilled a doctor שמואל was.

phrases.english: He placed it for him
in a tube of medicines
under his pillow,
and he was healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the problem left open after רבי refused both treatments.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל heals רבי with a painless method: medicine placed under his pillow.

steps.title: רבי tries to give שמואל סמיכה but fails
steps.stepSummary: רבי works hard to give שמואל סמיכה, but it never works out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי was troubling himself to ordain him, but the matter did not work out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי wants to give שמואל סמיכה and tries hard, but somehow it never happens. This sets up שמואל's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the healing, the story turns to a new issue. Even with all of רבי's effort, שמואל never gets סמיכה. The next step begins to explain why.

phrases.english: Rebbi was troubling himself to ordain him
but the matter did not work out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of שמואל and רבי with a new problem.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי's attempts to give שמואל סמיכה keep failing.

steps.title: שמואל says it is written in אדם הראשון's book
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells רבי not to be upset, because he saw אדם הראשון's book and it says something about שמואל ירחינאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Let the master not be upset. I myself saw the book of אדם הראשון, and it is written in it: שמואל ירחינאה...
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל comforts רבי and starts to explain why the סמיכה keeps failing. The sentence continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says the failure is not רבי's fault. It was already written in the book of אדם הראשון. What exactly the book says about him comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: let the master not be upset
the book of the first man, אדם

phrases.english: He said to him: Let the master not be upset,
I myself saw
the book of Adam the first man,
and it is written in it: Shmuel Yarchina'a

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the סמיכה in step 38 kept failing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the failure as something already decided from heaven.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The failure might seem to be a problem with רבי's efforts.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was written long ago in אדם הראשון's book. The details continue on the next amud.
